image_description: A close-up macro shot of a brown butterfly, identified as a Ringlet (Aphantopus hyperantus), perched on a white flower with a yellow center. The butterfly's wings are held closed, displaying the ventral side which is light brown with distinct rows of black-ringed eyespots (ocelli). The body is fuzzy and brown. One antenna is clearly visible and clubbed. The background consists of soft-focus green foliage.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The left antenna is clearly visible, thin at the base and thickening into a distinct club at the tip, matching the diagnostic feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Satyrid butterfly with moderately sized wingspan.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The subject exhibits the general morphology of a Satyrid butterfly. While absolute size cannot be measured without a scale, the proportions relative to the flower head are consistent with a moderate wingspan (30-50mm).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings uniformly brown to dark brown with small eyespots (ocelli) arranged in rows.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible wing surface is a uniform tan/brown color. There is a clear row of black-ringed eyespots along the margin of the hindwing and smaller spots on the forewing, matching the description perfectly.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Wings held closed at rest revealing cryptic ventral patterning.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The butterfly is positioned with wings folded vertically above the body, exposing the underside (ventral) pattern typical for resting Satyrids.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brown body integument matching wing coloration.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The thorax and abdomen are covered in brown hairs that closely match the hue of the wing scales.
The thorax appears robust but the overall impression is of a standard butterfly body covered in dense setae (hair).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Reduced brush-like forelegs characteristic of nymphalids.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While Ringlets are Nymphalids and possess reduced forelegs, the angle of the image and the density of the body hair/flower petals obscure the specific leg attachments. It is impossible to definitively verify the 'brush-like' nature or reduction from this view.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Chitinous exoskeleton with segmented body (three tagmata).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The division between the head, thorax, and abdomen is visually discernible, consistent with insect anatomy.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification as 'Ringlet' and distinguish it from similar brown butterflies like Meadow Browns or Gatekeepers.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex wing margins/eyespots and the flower petals, ensuring the eyespots are structurally part of the wing and not floating artifacts.
To assess the naturalness of the texture on the hairy body and the sharpness of the eyespots, looking for subtle AI smearing or over-sharpening halos.
To verify the physical contact point between the legs/proboscis and the flower, ensuring no 'floating' geometry.

focus_areas: Integrity of eyespot rings (no melting or irregular shapes)
Texture consistency of body hair vs. wing scales
Boundary sharpness between wing edges and flower petals
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the eyespots on the hindwing. In AI generations, these often become elliptical or merge into the background. Verify they are perfect circles with distinct centers. Also, check the proboscis area; ensure it doesn't fuse with the flower stamen.
